title: Open covers detect native ringed pro-etale derived isomorphisms
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site; def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(j_i:V_i\to Z)_{i\in I}$ be a small family of open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] whose images cover $Z$. For each $i$, let $R_i$ be a ring sheaf on $V_i$ and let $c_i:j_i^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}R_i$ be an isomorphism, using the actual inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use native module inverse image with these coefficient isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then a morphism $a:K\to L$ in $D(R)$ is invertible if its derived inverse image under every $j_i$ is invertible. No boundedness, quasi-compactness, nonempty-cover, constructibility or constant-coefficient hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 0EYZ, section-localization, together with sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize, and derived.tex Tag 05RM, lemma-acyclic-general. Native-coefficient realization of step 8 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: Choose for each point z of Z one member j_i containing z. For each pro-etale object Q over Z, the first projections Q times_Z V_i to Q form an open cover: the pullback range formula lifts each point of Q to the chosen open over its image in Z. Each of those objects maps to the pro-etale object V_i over Z. Thus the sieve of objects factoring through the family V_i is covering on every Q, which is exactly CoversTop. Indexing the selected subfamily by points of Z keeps the universe of the covering family small. This also works when Z and the indexing family are empty. The point-lifting assertion is the image-of-base-change formula of lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image. The defining pro-etale topology contains Zariski covers, as implemented by ProEt.mem_topology_of_openImmersion.

For each open j_i, apply the canonical ringed open comparison to identify the unextended inverse image followed by a site-and-ring equivalence with module slice restriction. Scalar extension along c_i is naturally isomorphic to scalar restriction along its inverse, hence is the inverse of a scalar equivalence. If native pullback of a module map is invertible, that scalar equivalence reflects invertibility of the unextended inverse-image map. Applying the open-site equivalence and transporting by the ringed open comparison proves slice restriction of the module map invertible.

Apply the exact-pullback homology comparison in every degree n. Native inverse image is additive and exact for arbitrary inverse-image coefficient rings, so the assumed invertibility of the derived pullback map implies invertibility of native pullback of H^n(a). Step 2 converts this to invertibility of the slice restriction of H^n(a). Forgetting modules gives invertible restrictions of the underlying abelian-sheaf map on the family of step 1.

The sheaf cover-local isomorphism theorem glues the restricted inverses and proves the underlying sheaf map of H^n(a) invertible. The module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so H^n(a) is invertible. This holds separately for every integer n, with no bound or uniformity condition. The unbounded derived cohomology criterion then proves a invertible.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the covering-sieve argument in step 8 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent. Use the existing exact homology comparison and the sheaf cover-local isomorphism theorem directly, avoiding separate derived-category instances on every slice.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleRingedOpenCover_reflectsIso {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Z) CommRingCat.{u + 1}) (ι : Type (u + 1))
    (V : ι → Scheme.{u}) (j : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Z) [∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)]
    (cover : ∀ z : Z, ∃ (i : ι) (v : V i), (j i).base v = z)
    (R' : ∀ i, Sheaf (ProEt.topology (V i)) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : ∀ i, (proEtaleSheafInverseImage (j i) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R ≅ R' i)
    {K L : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules Z R)} (a : K ⟶ L)
    (localIso : ∀ i,
      IsIso ((proEtaleRingModulePullback (j i) R (R' i) (c i)).mapDerivedCategory.map a)) :
    IsIso a
